**[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

**Execution Date: August 18, 2023**

This Agreement resolves all disputes between the Parties in connection with *Cardinal Peak Industries v. Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.*, Case No. 2022-L-008471, Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, County Department, Law Division

This Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (this \"**Agreement**\") is entered into as of August 18, 2023 (the \"**Effective Date**\"), by and between:

**Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 4200 West Lakeshore Industrial Parkway, Suite 300, Waukegan, Illinois 60085 (EIN: 36-4821097; Delaware Charter No. 7284159) (hereinafter \"**Nexford**\" or \"**NIH**\");

and

**Cardinal Peak Industries**, a Colorado limited liability company with its principal place of business at 1580 Ridgeline Boulevard, Pueblo, Colorado 81001 (EIN: 84-3295618) (hereinafter \"**Cardinal Peak**\" or \"**CPI**\").

Nexford and Cardinal Peak are each referred to individually herein as a \"**Party**\" and collectively as the \"**Parties**.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, Nexford and Cardinal Peak are parties to that certain Master Supply Agreement dated January 15, 2020, designated MSA-NIH-CPI-2020-001 (the \"**MSA**\"), pursuant to which Cardinal Peak manufactures and supplies hot-rolled coil (\"**HRC**\") and cold-rolled coil (\"**CRC**\") steel products to Nexford for use in Nexford\'s downstream fabrication and distribution operations;

**WHEREAS**, the MSA provides for the pass-through of certain raw-material surcharges, including scrap surcharges, energy surcharges, and alloy surcharges, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in Section 7.4 of the MSA and the methodology prescribed in Exhibit C thereto (the \"**Surcharge Methodology**\"), which methodology specifies, among other things, the applicable indices, baseline reference points, calculation periods, and cap-and-collar mechanisms governing the determination of such surcharges;

**WHEREAS**, a dispute arose between the Parties concerning surcharge invoices issued by Cardinal Peak for the period from March 2021 through May 2022 (the \"**Disputed Period**\"), during which Cardinal Peak invoiced total surcharges of approximately Six Million Four Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars (\$6,410,000.00), of which Nexford paid One Million Six Hundred Eighty Thousand Dollars (\$1,680,000.00), and Cardinal Peak claims an unpaid balance of approximately Four Million Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$4,730,000.00) (the \"**Surcharge Dispute**\");

**WHEREAS**, at the core of the Surcharge Dispute, Nexford contends that Cardinal Peak deviated from the Surcharge Methodology by, among other things, utilizing incorrect index reference dates, applying surcharges to product categories excluded from the surcharge pass-through framework, and failing to apply the cap-and-collar limitations set forth in Exhibit C, while Cardinal Peak contends that its surcharge calculations were proper and in accordance with the MSA as reasonably interpreted;

**WHEREAS**, on June 10, 2022, Cardinal Peak, through its counsel Blackwood Stein & Associates LLP, issued a formal demand to Nexford for payment of Four Million Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$4,730,000.00), which demand included a detailed reconciliation of surcharge invoices for the Disputed Period, and Nexford, through its General Counsel Deborah Whitfield, rejected such demand by letter dated July 5, 2022, setting forth Nexford\'s position that a substantial portion of the surcharges had been improperly calculated;

**WHEREAS**, on August 8, 2022, Cardinal Peak filed a Complaint against Nexford in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, County Department, Law Division, docketed as Case No. 2022-L-008471 (the \"**Litigation**\"), asserting claims for breach of contract (Count I), unjust enrichment (Count II), and account stated (Count III), and seeking damages in the amount of \$4,730,000.00, plus pre-judgment interest, costs, and attorneys\' fees;

**WHEREAS**, on September 19, 2022, Nexford, through its counsel Calderwood & Harkness LLP, filed an Answer and Affirmative Defenses to the Complaint, raising, among other defenses, failure to comply with contractual conditions precedent, failure to mitigate, estoppel, and the contractual cap-and-collar limitations, and on October 3, 2022, Nexford filed a Counterclaim (the \"**Counterclaim**\") asserting breach of contract by Cardinal Peak and seeking declaratory judgment that Cardinal Peak\'s surcharge calculations were inconsistent with the Surcharge Methodology, as well as recovery of alleged overpayments in the approximate amount of Two Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars (\$210,000.00);

**WHEREAS**, the Parties have engaged in extensive discovery in the Litigation, including the exchange of thousands of pages of documents, interrogatory responses, and requests for admission, as well as depositions of fact witnesses and the exchange of expert reports addressing the proper interpretation and application of the Surcharge Methodology, and have thereby fully informed themselves of the facts and law relating to the Surcharge Dispute;

**WHEREAS**, the MSA, at Section 14.3, provides for mandatory mediation in Chicago, Illinois, administered by a mutually agreed-upon neutral mediator, as a prerequisite to the continuation of litigation, and on May 22, 2023, the Parties jointly moved to stay the Litigation pending mediation, which motion was granted by the Honorable Judge Raymond P. Callahan on June 5, 2023;

**WHEREAS**, on August 2, 2023, the Parties participated in a full-day mediation session before the Honorable Catherine Lindström (Ret.) at the Great Lakes Dispute Resolution Center, 150 North Riverside Plaza, Suite 2700, Chicago, Illinois 60606, at which session the Parties, after extensive arms-length negotiation, reached an agreement in principle to resolve the Surcharge Dispute, the material terms of which were memorialized in a term sheet signed by authorized representatives of both Parties on August 2, 2023 (the \"**Term Sheet**\");

**WHEREAS**, the Parties desire to fully and finally resolve and settle the Litigation, including all claims asserted in the Complaint and the Counterclaim, and all other disputes, claims, and controversies between them arising out of or relating to the MSA, the Surcharge Dispute, and the Disputed Period, without any admission of liability, wrongdoing, or fault by either Party, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement;

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged by each Party, the Parties hereby agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE 1 --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article 1 shall have the meanings given to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

**1.1 \"Agreement\"** means this Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release, including all exhibits and schedules attached hereto, as the same may be amended or supplemented from time to time in accordance with Section 9.4 hereof.

**1.2 \"Cardinal Peak Released Parties\"** means Cardinal Peak Industries, together with its members, managers, officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, affiliates, subsidiaries, successors, and assigns, including without limitation the following individuals in their individual and corporate capacities: Frank Delacroix, Natalie Gunderson, Harold Briggs, and Patricia Morrow.

**1.3 \"Counterclaim\"** means the Counterclaim filed by Nexford on October 3, 2022 in the Litigation, including all claims for breach of contract, declaratory relief, and recovery of alleged overpayments asserted therein, and any amendments thereto.

**1.4 \"Disputed Period\"** means the period commencing March 1, 2021 and ending May 31, 2022, inclusive.

**1.5 \"Effective Date\"** means August 18, 2023, the date of execution of this Agreement by both Parties.

**1.6 \"Litigation\"** means the lawsuit styled *Cardinal Peak Industries v. Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.*, Case No. 2022-L-008471, pending in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, County Department, Law Division, including all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, third-party claims, motions, and proceedings filed or initiated therein.

**1.7 \"MSA\"** means the Master Supply Agreement dated January 15, 2020, reference number MSA-NIH-CPI-2020-001, entered into between Nexford and Cardinal Peak, together with all exhibits, schedules, amendments, and addenda thereto.

**1.8 \"Nexford Released Parties\"** means Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc., together with its officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, affiliates (including without limitation Marlowe Asset Management Bluff Capital Partners, LP and Marlowe Asset Management Bluff Capital Management LLC), subsidiaries, successors, and assigns, including without limitation the following individuals in their individual and corporate capacities: Martin Schaeffer, Lydia Tran, Russell Okonkwo, and Deborah Whitfield.

**1.9 \"Settlement Amount\"** means the aggregate sum of One Million Eight Hundred Ninety Thousand Dollars (\$1,890,000.00), as further described in Article 2 hereof.

**1.10 \"Term Sheet\"** means the term sheet signed by authorized representatives of both Parties on August 2, 2023, at the conclusion of the mediation session before the Honorable Catherine Lindström (Ret.). Upon execution of this Agreement, the Term Sheet is superseded in its entirety by this Agreement and shall have no further force or effect.

**[ARTICLE 2 --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**2.1 Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims, counterclaims, demands, and causes of action asserted or that could have been asserted in the Litigation or otherwise arising out of or relating to the Surcharge Dispute, the MSA (including Section 7.4, Exhibit C, and the Surcharge Methodology), and the Disputed Period, Nexford shall pay to Cardinal Peak the aggregate sum of One Million Eight Hundred Ninety Thousand Dollars (\$1,890,000.00) (the \"**Settlement Amount**\"). The Parties acknowledge that the Settlement Amount represents approximately forty percent (40%) of the Four Million Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$4,730,000.00) claimed by Cardinal Peak in the Litigation and has been negotiated at arms\' length, through mediation, and reflects a compromise of the Parties\' respective claims and defenses. Payment of the Settlement Amount, in accordance with the terms set forth herein, shall constitute full satisfaction of all obligations of Nexford to Cardinal Peak arising out of or relating to the Surcharge Dispute and the Litigation.

**2.2 Payment Schedule.** The Settlement Amount shall be paid by Nexford to Cardinal Peak in two (2) installments, as follows:

> **(a) First Installment.** One Million One Hundred Thirty-Four Thousand Dollars (\$1,134,000.00), representing sixty percent (60%) of the Settlement Amount, shall be due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date, that is, no later than September 17, 2023.
>
> **(b) Second Installment.** Seven Hundred Fifty-Six Thousand Dollars (\$756,000.00), representing forty percent (40%) of the Settlement Amount, shall be due and payable within ninety (90) calendar days of the Effective Date, that is, no later than November 16, 2023.

**[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

**(Execution Version)**

**April 22, 2024**

*Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al.* Case No. 1021-00006 Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida

CONFIDENTIAL --- SUBJECT TO CONFIDENTIALITY PROVISIONS OF ARTICLE XII

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE**

This **SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE** (this \"Agreement\") is entered into and made effective as of April 22, 2024 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among the following parties:

**VERIMARK HOSPITALITY GROUP INC.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal place of business at 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, and whose common stock is listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol \"VHMK\" (hereinafter referred to as \"Verimark\" or \"VHG\");

and

**COASTAL PALMS FRANCHISE HOLDINGS LLC**, a Florida limited liability company, with its principal office at 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108 (hereinafter referred to as \"Coastal Palms\" or \"CPFH\");

**RANDALL \"RANDY\" BRECKER**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who serves as the Managing Member and holds a sixty percent (60%) equity interest in Coastal Palms, and who also serves as the President of Suncoast Room Management Inc. (hereinafter referred to as \"R. Brecker\");

**THERESA BRECKER**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who is a Member of and holds a fifteen percent (15%) equity interest in Coastal Palms (hereinafter referred to as \"T. Brecker\");

**NOLAN PRESCOTT**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who is a Member of and holds a twenty-five percent (25%) equity interest in Coastal Palms (hereinafter referred to as \"Prescott\");

**GULF BREEZE HOSPITALITY LLC**, a Florida limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as \"Gulf Breeze\");

**SAVANNAH LODGING PARTNERS LLC**, a Georgia limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as \"Savannah Lodging\");

**SUNCOAST ROOM MANAGEMENT INC.**, a Florida corporation (hereinafter referred to as \"Suncoast\");

Coastal Palms, R. Brecker, T. Brecker, Prescott, Gulf Breeze, Savannah Lodging, and Suncoast are collectively referred to herein as the \"Coastal Palms Parties.\" Verimark and the Coastal Palms Parties are collectively referred to herein as the \"Parties\" and each individually as a \"Party.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS:**

**A. Franchise Relationship.** Verimark operates and franchises approximately 340 branded hotel properties across the southeastern United States under the \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand\" flags. For fiscal year 2021, Verimark reported consolidated revenue of approximately \$1.42 billion, of which the franchise segment contributed approximately \$218 million. Coastal Palms is the operator of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties --- eighteen (18) operating under the Verimark Suites flag and four (4) operating under the Verimark Select flag --- located across the States of Florida and Georgia, comprising approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. The first Franchise License Agreement (\"FLA\") between Verimark and Coastal Palms was executed on June 15, 2007, for a Verimark Suites property located in Naples, Florida. Over the following years, Coastal Palms and its affiliates executed a total of twenty-two (22) individual FLAs with Verimark, the most recent of which was dated September 3, 2019. Each FLA provides for a twenty (20)-year initial term and is governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any disputes in Broward County, Florida. Under each FLA, Coastal Palms is required to pay the following fees: (i) a royalty equal to five percent (5%) of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") (FLA § 4.1); (ii) a marketing-fund contribution equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR (FLA § 4.2); and (iii) a technology fee of twelve dollars and fifty cents (\$12.50) per available room per month, adjusted annually for changes in the Consumer Price Index, with such adjustment capped at three percent (3%) per year (FLA § 4.3). Late-payment interest under the FLAs accrues at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly (FLA § 4.6). Additionally, FLA § 15.3 provides for liquidated damages upon termination for cause in an amount equal to three times (3×) the trailing-twelve-month royalties per property.

**B. The Litigation.** On November 8, 2021, a former Coastal Palms regional controller, Janet Kerrigan, reported to Verimark\'s compliance hotline allegations of systematic revenue underreporting by the Coastal Palms Parties. In response, Verimark retained Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP to conduct a franchise-compliance audit of the Coastal Palms properties. Thornbury\'s preliminary findings, delivered to Verimark on January 18, 2022, indicated that the audited properties had underreported GRR by approximately twenty-six percent (26%) for the period spanning fiscal years 2019 through 2021. Verimark issued a Notice of Material Breach to Coastal Palms on February 4, 2022, demanding that Coastal Palms cure the identified breaches within thirty (30) days in accordance with FLA § 14.1. Coastal Palms, through its counsel Whitfield, Barrow & Crane LLP, responded by letter dated February 28, 2022, denying any material breach and contesting the methodology and conclusions of the Thornbury audit. No cure was tendered by Coastal Palms within the thirty (30)-day period, which expired on March 6, 2022. On March 7, 2022, Verimark filed a ten-count Complaint in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, bearing Case Number 1021-00006 (the \"Litigation\"), asserting claims for: (i) breach of contract --- royalties; (ii) breach of contract --- marketing fund; (iii) breach of contract --- technology fees; (iv) breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing; (v) fraudulent concealment; (vi) negligent misrepresentation; (vii) unjust enrichment; (viii) declaratory judgment; (ix) accounting; and (x) civil conspiracy. In the Complaint, Verimark claimed damages in the approximate aggregate amount of \$150,000,000, consisting of: (a) \$16,095,000 in direct underpayments of royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees; (b) \$28,400,000 in contractual late-payment interest calculated in accordance with FLA § 4.6; and (c) \$105,500,000 in liquidated damages calculated in accordance with FLA § 15.3. On April 18, 2022, Coastal Palms filed its Answer, Affirmative Defenses, and Counterclaim, asserting a counterclaim in the amount of \$12,000,000 for alleged brand-standard violations by Verimark and alleged over-billing for technology services. During discovery, Verimark\'s forensic accounting expert, Dr. Sharon Kettlewell, CPA/CFF, CFE, of Ridgeline Forensic Advisory LLC, prepared an expert report estimating cumulative underreported GRR of \$197,800,000 over the period from 2013 through 2021. Coastal Palms\' damages expert, Professor Grant Hargrove, PhD, CPA, of Hargrove Economic Consulting Inc., prepared a competing expert report opining that any underpayment totaled no more than \$6,200,000.

**C. Summary Judgment Ruling.** On February 9, 2024, the Court (the Honorable Richard M. Calloway, Circuit Judge) entered an Order granting Verimark\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on Count I (Breach of Contract --- Royalties) and Count II (Breach of Contract --- Marketing Fund), finding as a matter of law that Coastal Palms\' exclusion of revenues collected by Suncoast Room Management Inc. from its calculation and reporting of GRR constituted a material breach of FLA §§ 4.1 and 4.2. The Court denied Coastal Palms\' Cross-Motion for Summary Judgment on all counts and deferred the determination of damages to trial.

**D. Mediation and Settlement.** On February 23, 2024, the Parties agreed to submit their dispute to mediation before the Honorable Patricia Everwood (Retired), of Everwood Dispute Resolution PLLC. A two-day mediation session was conducted on March 14 and 15, 2024, at 396 Alhambra Circle, Suite 800, Coral Gables, Florida 33134. A tentative settlement was reached on the second day of mediation, March 15, 2024, and the Parties executed a written term sheet memorializing the principal terms of the settlement on March 22, 2024. The Parties now desire to fully and finally resolve all claims and counterclaims in the Litigation, and all related disputes among the Parties, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement.

**E. Desire to Settle.** The Parties acknowledge the uncertainty, risk, and expense inherent in continued litigation and trial, and each Party has made an independent assessment of the merits and risks of its respective claims and defenses. The Parties desire to avoid the further burden and expense of trial and to resolve their disputes amicably and in full. Entry into this Agreement is not, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, wrongdoing, or the validity of any claim or defense by any Party. Each Party has been represented by competent legal counsel of its choosing in the negotiation and execution of this Agreement, and each Party has had a full and fair opportunity to review, analyze, and negotiate the terms set forth herein.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, releases, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article I shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

**1.1** \"**Agreement**\" means this Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release, together with all Exhibits and Schedules attached hereto, which are incorporated herein by reference and made a part hereof.

**1.2** \"**Closing**\" means the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement on the Closing Date, including the execution and delivery of this Agreement by all Parties, the payment of the Initial Payment, and the execution and delivery of all ancillary documents required to be delivered at or prior to the Closing.

**1.3** \"**Closing Date**\" means April 22, 2024.

**1.4** \"**Collateral Properties**\" means the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties identified in Schedule 3.1 hereto, which serve as collateral for the security interest granted to Verimark pursuant to Article III.

**1.5** \"**Complaint**\" means the ten-count Complaint filed by Verimark on March 7, 2022, in Case No. 1021-00006, in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, together with all amendments thereto.

**1.6** \"**Counterclaim**\" means the \$12,000,000 counterclaim filed by Coastal Palms on April 18, 2022, in the Litigation, asserting claims for alleged brand-standard violations and over-billing.

**1.7** \"**Court**\" means the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida.

**1.8** \"**De-Identification Deadline**\" means August 20, 2024, which is one hundred twenty (120) days from the Closing Date.

**1.9** \"**Enhanced Audit Protocol**\" means the enhanced audit and reporting requirements applicable to the Retained Properties, as set forth in Article VIII of this Agreement and as more fully described in Exhibit D attached hereto.

**1.10** \"**Event of Default**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.7 of this Agreement.

**1.11** \"**Existing FLAs**\" means the twenty-two (22) Franchise License Agreements between Verimark and Coastal Palms and/or its affiliates (including Gulf Breeze and Savannah Lodging), the first of which was executed on June 15, 2007, and the most recent of which was executed on September 3, 2019, governing the operation of the Properties under the Verimark Brands.

**1.12** \"**GRR**\" or \"**Gross Room Revenue**\" has the meaning ascribed to such term in Section 4.1 of each FLA, which generally includes all revenue derived from or attributable to the rental of guest rooms at the applicable Property, regardless of the method of collection, booking channel, or collecting entity.

**1.13** \"**Initial Payment**\" means the cash payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) payable by Coastal Palms to Verimark at Closing in accordance with Section 2.2 of this Agreement.

**1.14** \"**Ironclad**\" means Ironclad National Bank, a national banking association, which holds first-lien mortgage loans on eighteen (18) of the twenty-two (22) Properties, with an aggregate outstanding principal balance of approximately Ninety-Four Million Dollars (\$94,000,000) as of the date hereof.

**1.15** \"**Litigation**\" means the action styled *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al.*, Case No. 1021-00006, pending in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, including all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and third-party claims asserted therein.

**1.16** \"**New FLAs**\" means the new ten (10)-year Franchise License Agreements to be executed by Verimark and the applicable Coastal Palms Party for each of the Retained Properties, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit C.

**1.17** \"**Payment Schedule**\" means the schedule of payments set forth in Article II and as more fully described in Exhibit A attached hereto.

**1.18** \"**Personal Guaranties**\" means the individual guaranty agreements to be executed by R. Brecker and Prescott, each substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit E, pursuant to which R. Brecker and Prescott jointly and severally guarantee all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement.

**1.19** \"**Properties**\" means the twenty-two (22) hotel properties operated by the Coastal Palms Parties under the Existing FLAs.

**1.20** \"**Retained Properties**\" means the eight (8) Properties identified in Section 7.1 of this Agreement and in Exhibit C that will continue to be franchised under the New FLAs, consisting of four (4) properties in Naples, Florida; two (2) properties on Marco Island, Florida; and two (2) properties in Tampa, Florida.

**1.21** \"**Security Agreement**\" means the security agreement to be executed by Coastal Palms in favor of Verimark, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F, granting Verimark a first-priority security interest in the Collateral Properties to secure the Structured Payments and other obligations under this Agreement.

**1.22** \"**Settlement Amount**\" means the aggregate sum of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), payable by the Coastal Palms Parties to Verimark in accordance with Article II of this Agreement.

**1.23** \"**Structured Payments**\" means the eight (8) semi-annual payments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in accordance with Section 2.3 of this Agreement, the first such payment being due on October 22, 2024, and the last such payment being due on April 22, 2028, as more fully described in the Payment Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit A.

**1.24** \"**Surrendered Properties**\" means the fourteen (14) Properties identified in Section 7.1 and Exhibit B of this Agreement that are subject to franchise surrender, de-identification, and termination of the applicable Existing FLAs.

**1.25** \"**Verimark Brands**\" means \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand,\" together with all associated trademarks, service marks, logos, trade dress, proprietary systems (including reservation systems, property management systems, and revenue management systems), and all other intellectual property owned, licensed, or controlled by Verimark in connection with the branding and operation of its franchised hotel properties.

**[ARTICLE II --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Total Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims, counterclaims, causes of action, and disputes among the Parties, whether asserted or unasserted, known or unknown, arising from or relating to the Existing FLAs, the Litigation, or the subject matter thereof, the Coastal Palms Parties shall pay to Verimark a total Settlement Amount of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), payable as follows:

> \(a\) The Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), payable at the Closing in accordance with Section 2.2 below; and
>
> \(b\) The Structured Payments totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in eight (8) semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, in accordance with Section 2.3 below.

The Payment Schedule setting forth the dates, amounts, and interest calculations for all payments under this Article II is attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference.

**Section 2.2 --- Initial Payment.** On the Closing Date, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) by wire transfer of immediately available funds from the escrow account established at Ironclad National Bank for the purposes of this settlement to Verimark\'s designated account. Verimark shall provide Coastal Palms with complete wire-transfer instructions for the designated receiving account no later than three (3) business days prior to the Closing Date. Upon receipt of the Initial Payment, Verimark\'s counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, at 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, shall promptly issue a written confirmation of receipt to counsel for the Coastal Palms Parties. The obligation to make the Initial Payment is unconditional and shall not be subject to any right of setoff, counterclaim, defense, or deduction.

**Section 2.3 --- Structured Payments.** Following the payment of the Initial Payment, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the remaining Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000) in eight (8) equal semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, on the following schedule:

> \(a\) The first installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2024.
>
> \(b\) The second installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2025.
>
> \(c\) The third installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2025.
>
> \(d\) The fourth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2026.
>
> \(e\) The fifth installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2026.
>
> \(f\) The sixth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2027.
>
> \(g\) The seventh installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2027.
>
> \(h\) The eighth and final installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2028.

All Structured Payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Verimark in accordance with the wire-transfer instructions provided pursuant to Section 2.2, or to such other account as Verimark may designate in writing from time to time upon not less than ten (10) business days\' prior notice to Coastal Palms.

**Section 2.4 --- Interest on Structured Payments.** Interest shall accrue on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments at a rate of six and one-half percent (6.5%) per annum, simple interest, calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed. Interest shall begin to accrue on the Closing Date and shall be calculated on the then-outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments. Interest payments shall be due and payable concurrently with each semi-annual installment payment. The amount of interest due with each installment shall be calculated by multiplying the outstanding principal balance as of the first day of the applicable interest period by the annual interest rate of 6.5%, and then multiplying the result by a fraction, the numerator of which is the actual number of days elapsed during such interest period and the denominator of which is 365. A detailed schedule setting forth the estimated interest amounts due with each installment is set forth in Exhibit A.

**Section 2.5 --- Late Payments.** Any Structured Payment (including any concurrent interest payment) not received by Verimark within ten (10) business days of its scheduled due date shall bear additional default interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month on the overdue amount, calculated from the original due date until the date on which such overdue amount is received by Verimark in full. This default interest shall be in addition to, and not in substitution for, the interest otherwise payable under Section 2.4. If Coastal Palms fails to cure a late payment within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the overdue payment and the amount due, such failure shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 2.7 of this Agreement. Nothing in this Section 2.5 shall be construed to extend the due date for any Structured Payment or to waive Verimark\'s right to declare an Event of Default following the expiration of the applicable cure period.

**Section 2.6 --- Prepayment.** Coastal Palms may, at its option, prepay all or any portion of the Structured Payments at any time without premium, penalty, or additional charge of any kind. Any partial prepayment shall be applied first to any accrued and unpaid interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, and second to the scheduled installments in inverse order of maturity (i.e., applied first to the most distant scheduled installment, then to the next most distant, and so on), thereby reducing the total interest obligation over the remaining term. Coastal Palms shall provide Verimark with not less than five (5) business days\' prior written notice of any prepayment, specifying the amount and intended date of such prepayment. Verimark shall recalculate the interest amounts due on any remaining installments following any partial prepayment and shall provide an updated Payment Schedule to Coastal Palms within ten (10) business days of receipt of any such prepayment.

**Section 2.7 --- Events of Default and Acceleration.** An \"Event of Default\" shall be deemed to have occurred upon the happening of any of the following:

> \(a\) **Payment Default.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to make any payment of the Structured Payments, accrued interest, or any other monetary obligation under this Agreement within thirty (30) days of the date on which Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such payment default;
>
> \(b\) **Covenant Default.** Breach by any Coastal Palms Party of any material covenant, agreement, or obligation under this Agreement (other than a payment obligation, which is governed by clause (a) above) that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such breach in reasonable detail;
>
> \(c\) **Bankruptcy or Insolvency.** The commencement of any voluntary or involuntary proceeding under the United States Bankruptcy Code, Title 11, United States Code, or under any state insolvency, receivership, dissolution, or similar statute, by or against any Coastal Palms Party, or the appointment of a receiver, trustee, custodian, or similar official for the business, assets, or property of any Coastal Palms Party, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors by any Coastal Palms Party;
>
> \(d\) **Breach of Representations and Warranties.** Any representation or warranty made by any Coastal Palms Party in this Agreement or in any ancillary document delivered in connection herewith that is materially inaccurate, false, or misleading as of the date on which it was made, and such inaccuracy, falsity, or misleading character is not cured within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the same;
>
> \(e\) **De-Identification Failure.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to comply with the de-identification requirements set forth in Article VII of this Agreement by the De-Identification Deadline.

Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Verimark may, at its sole election and upon written notice to Coastal Palms, declare the entire outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon and all other amounts owing under this Agreement, immediately due and payable in full, without further notice, demand, presentment, or protest, all of which are hereby waived by the Coastal Palms Parties. Acceleration of the Structured Payments pursuant to this Section 2.7 shall not constitute a waiver of, or limit, any other rights or remedies available to Verimark at law or in equity, including, without limitation, the right to enforce the Security Agreement, to seek collection under the Personal Guaranties, to pursue foreclosure on the Collateral Properties, and to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from the Court.

**Section 2.8 --- Tax Treatment.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of all federal, state, and local taxes, and for the filing of all tax returns and reports, arising from or attributable to the payments received or made by such Party under this Agreement. NEW YORK SUPREME COURT COUNTY OF NEW YORK MATRIMONIAL PART 7

**SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND STIPULATION OF SETTLEMENT**

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **JONATHAN R. CALDWELL,**                   
  ------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------
  Petitioner,                                 **Index No. 312847/2022**

  -against-                                   **Before: Hon. Patricia K. Lessing, J.S.C.**

  **DR. ELENA M. CALDWELL (née Baranova),**   

  Respondent.                                 
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Date of Execution: May 12, 2023

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**[PREAMBLE]{.underline}**

This Settlement Agreement and Stipulation of Settlement (hereinafter, the \"Agreement\") is made and entered into as of the 12th day of May, 2023, by and between:

**JONATHAN R. CALDWELL** (\"Husband\" or \"Petitioner\"), age 52, born March 17, 1970, presently residing at 14 Gramercy Park South, Apt. PH-A, New York, New York 10003,

and

**DR. ELENA M. CALDWELL**, née Baranova (\"Wife\" or \"Respondent\"), age 48, born September 4, 1974, presently residing at 320 West 76th Street, Apt. 12B, New York, New York 10023.

The Husband and the Wife are sometimes referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, the Parties were lawfully married on June 21, 2008, in the City, County, and State of New York, and the marriage has been of approximately fourteen (14) years\' duration; and

**WHEREAS**, two (2) minor children were born of the marriage, namely: Sophia Caldwell, born February 12, 2012, presently age eleven (11), and Alexander Caldwell, born August 29, 2014, presently age nine (9) (collectively, the \"Children\"); and

**WHEREAS**, the Parties separated on or about April 3, 2022, when the Wife vacated the marital residence located at 14 Gramercy Park South, Apt. PH-A, New York, New York 10003, and established a separate residence at 320 West 76th Street, Apt. 12B, New York, New York 10023; and

**WHEREAS**, the Husband filed a Petition for Dissolution of Marriage on June 14, 2022, and the action was assigned Index Number 312847/2022 in the Supreme Court of the State of New York, County of New York, Matrimonial Part 7, before the Honorable Patricia K. Lessing, Justice of the Supreme Court; and

**WHEREAS**, the Wife filed an Answer and Counterclaims on July 11, 2022, asserting, among other things, challenges to the validity and enforceability of the Prenuptial Agreement executed by the Parties on June 7, 2008; and

**WHEREAS**, prior to the marriage, the Parties executed a Prenuptial Agreement on June 7, 2008, fourteen (14) days prior to the wedding ceremony, at which time the Husband was represented by Gerald Sable, Esq. of Harwick & Sable LLP, 780 Third Avenue, Suite 3200, New York, New York 10017, and the Wife was represented by her own independent counsel, Miriam Fedorov, Esq. of Fedorov Law Office, 55 West 46th Street, Suite 901, New York, New York 10036; and

**WHEREAS**, in her Answer and Counterclaims, the Wife challenged the enforceability of the Prenuptial Agreement on the grounds of (a) inadequate financial disclosure by the Husband, (b) duress, and (c) unconscionability, and as part of this Settlement Agreement, the Wife voluntarily withdraws all such challenges to the validity and enforceability of the Prenuptial Agreement, and the Parties agree that the Prenuptial Agreement is valid and enforceable in its material terms; and

**WHEREAS**, the following proceedings have occurred in this matter:

> \(a\) A Preliminary Conference was held on August 22, 2022, before the Honorable Patricia K. Lessing, J.S.C.;
>
> \(b\) A pendente lite motion was decided on September 30, 2022, at which time the Court ordered temporary child support in the amount of \$14,000 per month; the Court denied temporary spousal maintenance and denied the Wife\'s application for exclusive occupancy of the marital residence;
>
> \(c\) Mutual discovery demands were served on November 15, 2022;
>
> \(d\) Expert reports were exchanged on January 18, 2023;
>
> \(e\) Depositions of both Parties were concluded on February 7, 2023;
>
> \(f\) Court-ordered mediation was conducted on March 14, 2023, and April 5, 2023, before the Honorable Robert Castellano (Ret.) of Castellano ADR Services LLC, 100 Church Street, Suite 800, New York, New York 10007; and
>
> \(g\) A settlement framework was reached at the second mediation session on April 5, 2023, and this Agreement memorializes and formalizes the terms of that settlement; and

**WHEREAS**, the Husband is represented in this action by Priya Anand, Esq. of Calderwood & Harkness LLP, 425 Lexington Avenue, 38th Floor, New York, New York 10017; and

**WHEREAS**, the Wife is represented in this action by Rachel Whitford, Esq. of Whitford Garza & Stein LLP, 600 Third Avenue, 22nd Floor, New York, New York 10016; and

**WHEREAS**, the Parties desire to settle all issues between them, including but not limited to equitable distribution of marital property, spousal maintenance, child support, child custody, and parenting time, and to resolve all claims and counterclaims arising out of or related to the marriage and the dissolution proceeding; and

**WHEREAS**, each Party acknowledges having had the opportunity to consult with independent legal counsel and independent financial advisors of his or her own choosing, and each Party has, in fact, retained and consulted with such counsel and advisors; and

**WHEREAS**, each Party enters into this Agreement voluntarily, free from fraud, duress, coercion, or undue influence of any kind, and with a full understanding of the nature, extent, and value of the marital estate and the rights being waived and retained herein; and

**WHEREAS**, the Parties intend that this Agreement shall be incorporated into and survive the Judgment of Divorce, and shall not be merged therein, so that the Agreement shall remain independently enforceable as a contract between the Parties;

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1.** As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them below, unless the context clearly requires otherwise:

**(a) \"Agreement\"** means this Settlement Agreement and Stipulation of Settlement, including all Schedules attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference.

**(b) \"Commencement Date\"** means June 14, 2022, the date on which the Husband filed the Petition for Dissolution of Marriage in this action.

**(c) \"Date of Marriage\"** means June 21, 2008, the date on which the Parties were lawfully married in the City, County, and State of New York.

**(d) \"Date of Separation\"** means April 3, 2022, the date on which the Wife vacated the marital residence and the Parties commenced living separate and apart from each other.

**(e) \"Effective Date\"** means the date on which the Judgment of Divorce is entered by the Court in this action.

**(f) \"Judgment of Divorce\"** means the final judgment of divorce entered by the Supreme Court of the State of New York, County of New York, in this action, Index Number 312847/2022.

**(g) \"Marital Property\"** means all property acquired by either or both of the Parties during the marriage with marital funds, regardless of the form in which title is held, as defined under New York Domestic Relations Law § 236(B)(1)(c) and as further set forth in the Prenuptial Agreement, excluding Separate Property as defined herein.

**(h) \"Separate Property\"** means all property owned by either Party prior to the Date of Marriage and all appreciation thereon (whether active or passive, except as otherwise specifically provided in this Agreement), as well as gifts, inheritances, and trust distributions received by either Party during the marriage, all as defined in the Prenuptial Agreement and under New York Domestic Relations Law § 236(B)(1)(d).

**(i) \"Prenuptial Agreement\"** means the prenuptial agreement executed by the Parties on June 7, 2008, prior to the Date of Marriage.

**(j) \"Children\"** means Sophia Caldwell, born February 12, 2012, and Alexander Caldwell, born August 29, 2014, the two minor children born of the marriage.

**(k) \"Marital Residence\"** means the real property and cooperative apartment unit located at 14 Gramercy Park South, Apt. PH-A, New York, New York 10003.

**(l) \"Vacation Property\"** means the real property located at 44 Dune Road, Westhampton Beach, New York 11978.

**(m) \"CMC\"** means Caldwell Meridian Capital LLC, a New York limited liability company with EIN 26-4831057, with its principal office at 590 Madison Avenue, 30th Floor, New York, New York 10022.

**(n) \"CRH\"** means Caldwell Realty Holdings LP, a New York limited partnership with EIN 27-1924683, with its principal office at 590 Madison Avenue, 30th Floor, New York, New York 10022.

**(o) \"CRH GP\"** means Caldwell Realty GP LLC, a New York limited liability company with EIN 27-1924690, the general partner of CRH.

**(p) \"Trident National Bank\"** means Trident National Bank, with offices at 277 Broadway, New York, New York 10007.

**(q) \"Mercer & Hall\"** means Mercer & Hall Securities LLC, with offices at 399 Park Avenue, 16th Floor, New York, New York 10022.

**(r) \"Graymoor Trust Company\"** means Graymoor Trust Company, with offices at 520 Madison Avenue, 14th Floor, New York, New York 10022.

**(s) \"QDRO\"** means a Qualified Domestic Relations Order as defined under Section 414(p) of the Internal Revenue Code and Section 206(d)(3) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended.

**(t) \"IRC\"** means the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.

**(u) \"DRL\"** means the New York Domestic Relations Law.

**Section 1.2.** All references to currency amounts in this Agreement are to United States Dollars. All references to \"days\" shall mean calendar days, unless otherwise specified. All references to statutes, rules, or regulations shall include any amendments thereto that may be enacted or promulgated from time to time.

**[ARTICLE II --- PRENUPTIAL AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Validity and Enforceability.** The Parties hereby agree and stipulate that the Prenuptial Agreement executed on June 7, 2008, is valid, binding, and enforceable in all respects. The Wife hereby withdraws, with prejudice, all claims and counterclaims set forth in her Answer and Counterclaims dated July 11, 2022, challenging the validity of the Prenuptial Agreement, including, without limitation, the claims of inadequate financial disclosure by the Husband, duress, and unconscionability. The Wife acknowledges that this withdrawal is made knowingly, voluntarily, and without reservation, as an integral component of the global settlement memorialized in this Agreement. The Wife further acknowledges that she has been advised by her counsel, Rachel Whitford, Esq., regarding the legal consequences of this withdrawal and waiver.

The terms of the Prenuptial Agreement shall govern the rights and obligations of the Parties to the extent consistent with the provisions of this Agreement. In the event that any provision of this Agreement expressly modifies, supersedes, or is inconsistent with a provision of the Prenuptial Agreement, the terms of this Agreement shall control. In all other respects, the Prenuptial Agreement shall remain in full force and effect.

**Section 2.2 --- Financial Disclosures.** The Parties acknowledge and confirm the financial disclosures made in connection with the execution of the Prenuptial Agreement on June 7, 2008. At that time, the Husband disclosed total assets of approximately \$25.2 million, as set forth in Schedule A attached to the Prenuptial Agreement and reproduced as Schedule A to this Agreement. At that time, the Wife disclosed total assets of approximately \$310,000, as set forth in Schedule B attached to the Prenuptial Agreement and reproduced as Schedule B to this Agreement. The Wife\'s withdrawal of her inadequate-disclosure claim is made knowingly and voluntarily as part of this global settlement, and the Wife acknowledges that the financial disclosures attached to the Prenuptial Agreement were substantially accurate as of their date.

**[ARTICLE III --- MARITAL ESTATE IDENTIFICATION AND VALUATION]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Total Marital Estate.** The Parties have engaged in extensive discovery, including the exchange of expert reports, forensic accounting analyses, and business valuations, and have conducted depositions of both Parties. Following arm\'s-length negotiations and mediation, the Parties have agreed, solely for purposes of this settlement, that the total marital estate is valued at approximately **\$89.17 million**. This agreed valuation represents a negotiated resolution of the dispute between the Husband\'s position that the total marital estate was valued at \$79.29 million and the Wife\'s position that the total marital estate was valued at \$108.81 million. The agreed valuation is not an admission by either Party as to the actual fair market value of any individual asset or the marital estate as a whole, but rather reflects the Parties\' compromise in the interest of resolving this matter without the need for trial.

**Section 3.2 --- Caldwell Meridian Capital LLC.**

**(a) Entity Description.** CMC is a New York limited liability company, Employer Identification Number 26-4831057, with its principal office at 590 Madison Avenue, 30th Floor, New York, New York 10022. CMC was founded on September 15, 2008, during the marriage, and is conceded by both Parties to be marital property.

**(b) Business Operations.** CMC is a registered investment advisor that manages diversified investment portfolios on behalf of institutional and high-net-worth individual clients. As of the most recent reporting period, CMC had approximately \$1.4 billion in assets under management.

**(c) Ownership.** The Husband holds an eighty-five percent (85%) ownership interest in CMC. The remaining fifteen percent (15%) is held by Derek Fong, who holds a ten percent (10%) interest, and Alicia Drummond, who holds a five percent (5%) interest.

**(d) Valuation Dispute.** The Husband\'s expert, Dr. Vivian Osei, CFA, ASA, of Pinnacle Valuation Group LLC, 110 William Street, Suite 2400, New York, New York 10038, valued the enterprise of CMC at \$38.2 million, resulting in a value of \$32.47 million for the Husband\'s 85% interest. The Wife\'s expert, Catherine Ng, CPA, of Ng Barker & Cole LLP, 1330 Avenue of the Americas, Suite 700, New York, New York 10019, valued the enterprise of CMC at \$52.7 million, resulting in a value of \$44.795 million for the Husband\'s 85% interest.

**(e) Agreed Settlement Valuation.** The Parties have agreed, solely for purposes of this settlement, that the value of the Husband\'s 85% membership interest in CMC is **\$36.55 million**.

**(f) Revenue and Compensation.** CMC derives revenue from annual management fees of approximately \$14.0 million (representing approximately 1.0% of assets under management) and incentive/performance fees, which in the 2021 fiscal year totaled approximately \$8.4 million. The Husband\'s total compensation from CMC in 2021 was approximately \$5.9 million, comprised of a salary of \$3.8 million and distributions of \$2.1 million.

**Section 3.3 --- Caldwell Realty Holdings LP.**

**(a) Entity Description.** CRH is a New York limited partnership, Employer Identification Number 27-1924683, with its principal office at 590 Madison Avenue, 30th Floor, New York, New York 10022. The general partner of CRH is CRH GP, a New York limited liability company, Employer Identification Number 27-1924690, which is one hundred percent (100%) owned by the Husband.

**(b) Portfolio.** CRH owns a total of twelve (12) real properties located across Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Westchester County. The total appraised value of the CRH portfolio is \$63.8 million. The total outstanding debt secured by the CRH properties, including balances due to Trident National Bank, is \$18.7 million. The aggregate net equity in the CRH portfolio is \$45.1 million.

**(c) Classification of Properties.**

> \(i\) *Pre-Marital Properties.* Three (3) of the twelve properties were acquired by the Husband prior to the Date of Marriage (the \"Pre-Marital CRH Properties\"). The Pre-Marital CRH Properties have a current appraised value of \$28.6 million, with allocated debt of \$6.2 million, yielding net equity of \$22.4 million. The Pre-Marital CRH Properties are treated as the Husband\'s Separate Property, subject to the active appreciation adjustment set forth in Section 3.4 below.
>
> \(ii\) *Marital Properties.* Nine (9) of the twelve properties were acquired during the marriage with marital funds (the \"Marital CRH Properties\"). The Marital CRH Properties have a current appraised value of \$35.2 million, with allocated debt of \$12.5 million, yielding net equity of \$22.7 million. The Marital CRH Properties are treated as Marital Property subject to equitable distribution.

**(d) Revolving Credit Facility.** CRH maintains a revolving credit facility with Trident National Bank, Facility Number TN-CRH-2017-09034, which is included in the aggregate outstanding debt referenced above.

**Section 3.4 --- Active vs. Passive Appreciation Resolution.**

The Wife had contended that the \$17.2 million in appreciation on the three Pre-Marital CRH Properties (valued at \$11.4 million at the time of the marriage and currently appraised at \$28.6 million) constituted active appreciation resulting from the Husband\'s management efforts during the marriage, and therefore constituted Marital Property subject to equitable distribution. The Husband maintained that the appreciation was passive and attributable to general market conditions, and therefore constituted Separate Property under the terms of the Prenuptial Agreement and DRL § 236(B)(1)(d).

As a compromise, and solely for purposes of this settlement, the Parties agree to treat **\$5.8 million** of the appreciation on the Pre-Marital CRH Properties as Marital Property subject to equitable distribution. The balance of the appreciation, totaling \$11.4 million, shall remain the Husband\'s Separate Property. This resolution reflects a negotiated compromise and is not an admission by either Party as to the characterization of the appreciation.

**Section 3.5 --- Marital Residence.**

**(a) Description.** The Marital Residence is the cooperative apartment unit located at 14 Gramercy Park South, Apt. PH-A, New York, New York 10003. Title to the shares and proprietary lease for the Marital Residence is held solely in the name of Jonathan R. Caldwell.

**(b) Acquisition.** The Marital Residence was purchased in March 2010, during the marriage, with marital funds, at a purchase price of \$6.9 million.

**(c) Current Valuation.** The current appraised value of the Marital Residence is \$11.4 million. The outstanding mortgage balance on the Marital Residence is \$4.1 million (Trident National Bank, Loan Number TN-2010-447821). The net equity in the Marital Residence is therefore \$7.3 million.

**[MUTUAL RELEASE AND SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

This Mutual Release and Settlement Agreement (this \"**Agreement**\") is entered into as of May 20, 2024 (the \"**Effective Date**\"), by and among:

**PELLEGRINO CAPITAL GROUP LLC**, a Florida limited liability company (\"**PCG**\"), with its principal office at 1900 Bayshore Boulevard, Suite 1400, Tampa, FL 33606;

**MERIDIAN SHORES HOSPITALITY LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company (\"**MSH**\"), with its principal office at 220 Royal Palm Way, Suite 300, Palm Beach, FL 33480;

**DOMINIC R. PELLEGRINO**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, in his capacity as Managing Member of PCG (\"**D. Pellegrino**\");

**NATHANIEL CORDERO**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, in his capacity as Managing Member of MSH (\"**N. Cordero**\"); and

**ELENA CORDERO**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, in her capacity as a Member of MSH (\"**E. Cordero**\").

PCG, MSH, D. Pellegrino, N. Cordero, and E. Cordero are each referred to herein as a \"**Party**\" and collectively as the \"**Parties**.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS:**

**A.** Palmetto Grand Ventures LLC (\"**PGV**\"), a Florida limited liability company (Florida Department of State Filing No. L17000124583; EIN: 82-5063921), was formed on June 15, 2017, pursuant to an Operating Agreement of Palmetto Grand Ventures LLC dated June 15, 2017 (the \"**Operating Agreement**\" or \"**OA**\"), by and between PCG and MSH, for the purposes and on the terms and conditions set forth therein;

**B.** Under the Operating Agreement, PCG holds a sixty-five percent (65%) membership interest in PGV and serves as the sole Manager of PGV, with exclusive authority over the day-to-day management, operations, and affairs of PGV, and MSH holds a thirty-five percent (35%) membership interest in PGV;

**C.** PGV was formed for the purpose of acquiring, renovating, and operating The Palmetto Grand Resort & Spa, a 312-room luxury beachfront hotel and resort located at 650 Mandalay Avenue, Clearwater Beach, FL 33767 (the \"**Property**\"), which PGV acquired on August 1, 2017, for a purchase price of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), funded in part by a loan from Gulf Atlantic National Bank (\"**GANB**\") in the original principal amount of Sixty-One Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$61,250,000) (Loan No. CRE-2017-06284) (the \"**GANB Loan**\");

**D.** The Property has been and continues to be operated under a franchise agreement with Aurelian Hotels & Resorts Inc. dated July 15, 2017 (the \"**Franchise Agreement**\"), which governs the brand standards, reservation systems, and operational requirements applicable to the Property;

**E.** On January 9, 2023, PCG delivered written notice to MSH exercising its call option under Section 12.4 of the Operating Agreement to purchase MSH\'s entire thirty-five percent (35%) membership interest in PGV at Fair Market Value, as that term is defined in Section 12.4(a) of the Operating Agreement;

**F.** In connection with its exercise of the call option, PCG retained Whitfield Realty Advisors LLC (\"**Whitfield**\") to prepare an independent appraisal of PGV\'s real property and operating assets, and Whitfield delivered an appraisal report dated February 15, 2023, concluding that the Fair Market Value of one hundred percent (100%) of PGV\'s real property and operating assets was One Hundred Eighteen Million Dollars (\$118,000,000) as of December 31, 2022;

**G.** Based on the Whitfield appraisal and the applicable provisions of the Operating Agreement, PCG calculated the buyout price for MSH\'s thirty-five percent (35%) membership interest as Forty-One Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$41,300,000), comprising Twenty-Four Million Two Hundred Ninety Thousand Dollars (\$24,290,000) attributable to MSH\'s thirty-five percent (35%) equity share and Seventeen Million Ten Thousand Dollars (\$17,010,000) in accrued preferred return, and tendered that amount to MSH on March 1, 2023;

**H.** MSH rejected PCG\'s tender on March 10, 2023, and independently retained Beacon Valuation Group Inc. (\"**Beacon**\") to prepare a competing appraisal of PGV\'s assets, and Beacon delivered an appraisal report dated March 5, 2023, concluding that the Fair Market Value of one hundred percent (100%) of PGV\'s assets was One Hundred Fifty-One Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$151,500,000) as of December 31, 2022, and MSH asserted a buyout price demand of Seventy Million Dollars (\$70,000,000), inclusive of a claimed bad-faith penalty under Section 12.7 of the Operating Agreement;

**I.** On March 20, 2023, MSH filed a Demand for Arbitration with JAMS (JAMS Ref. No. 1440032871), asserting claims against PCG for (i) bad-faith valuation under Section 12.7 of the Operating Agreement, (ii) breach of fiduciary duty by PCG in its capacity as Manager of PGV, and (iii) breach of Section 8.3 of the Operating Agreement regarding capital expenditure and deferred-maintenance obligations, including an alleged Eight Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$8,200,000) in deferred maintenance (the \"**Arbitration**\");

**J.** On April 5, 2023, PCG filed its Response and Counterclaim in the Arbitration, denying all of MSH\'s claims and seeking declaratory relief that the Forty-One Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollar (\$41,300,000) buyout price constituted the proper Fair Market Value under Section 12.4 of the Operating Agreement and that PCG had complied with all of its obligations thereunder;

**K.** Hon. Margaret Liu Chen (Ret.) was appointed as the sole arbitrator in the Arbitration on April 28, 2023, and a preliminary conference was held on May 15, 2023, at which the arbitrator established a procedural schedule for the conduct of the proceedings;

**L.** Pursuant to Section 12.4(c) of the Operating Agreement, which provides for the retention of a neutral third appraiser in the event the Parties\' respective appraisals diverge by more than fifteen percent (15%), the Parties jointly retained Linden Park Advisory LLC (\"**Linden Park**\") as such neutral third appraiser, and Linden Park delivered a preliminary indication of value in the range of One Hundred Thirty Million Dollars (\$130,000,000) to One Hundred Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$138,000,000) for one hundred percent (100%) of PGV\'s assets as of December 31, 2022;

**M.** The Parties engaged in extensive discovery in the Arbitration, including the production and exchange of documents, the taking of depositions of Gerald K. Whitfield (of Whitfield Realty Advisors LLC), Dr. Priya Ramanathan (of Beacon Valuation Group Inc.), Dominic R. Pellegrino, and Nathaniel Cordero, and briefing on a motion to compel production of certain financial records and internal communications, which motion was partially granted by the arbitrator on November 30, 2023;

**N.** On January 15, 2024, the Parties agreed to submit their dispute to mediation, and the Parties participated in two mediation sessions with Raymond Alcazar of Alcazar Dispute Resolution LLC, the first held on February 12, 2024, and the second held on March 25, 2024, at which the Parties reached a framework for settlement of all outstanding claims and disputes;

**O.** On April 8, 2024, the Parties executed a binding Term Sheet (the \"**Term Sheet**\") setting forth the principal terms of the settlement, including the agreed-upon redemption price, the structure of the redemption transaction, and the mutual release of all claims;

**P.** Contemporaneously with the execution of this Agreement, the Parties are executing a Redemption Agreement dated May 20, 2024 (the \"**Redemption Agreement**\"), providing for PCG\'s purchase of MSH\'s entire thirty-five percent (35%) membership interest in PGV for a redemption price of Fifty-Two Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$52,850,000) (the \"**Redemption Price**\"), on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth therein; and

**Q.** The Parties desire to fully and finally settle, compromise, and resolve any and all claims, disputes, controversies, and causes of action between and among them arising out of or relating to the Operating Agreement, the call-option exercise, the Arbitration, and PGV, on the terms and conditions set forth herein, and to provide for the mutual release of all such claims so that the Parties may conclude their business relationship with finality and certainty.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, releases, and agreements contained herein, the payment of the Redemption Price pursuant to the Redemption Agreement, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged by each of the Parties, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1 --- Definitions.** As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article I shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

> \(a\) \"**Arbitration**\" means the arbitration proceeding captioned *Meridian Shores Hospitality LLC v. Pellegrino Capital Group LLC*, JAMS Ref. No. 1440032871, pending before Hon. Margaret Liu Chen (Ret.) in Jacksonville, Florida.
>
> \(b\) \"**Claims**\" means any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, expenses (including attorneys\' fees and disbursements), obligations, judgments, liens, penalties, fines, debts, accounts, offsets, rights, promises, agreements, and controversies, of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, disclosed or undisclosed, matured or unmatured, accrued or unaccrued, contingent or fixed, liquidated or unliquidated, at law or in equity, arising under statute, contract, tort, or any other legal or equitable theory, whether arising under federal, state, or local law.
>
> \(c\) \"**Effective Date**\" means May 20, 2024.
>

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800 Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301 Telephone: (954) 555-7200 \| Facsimile: (954) 555-7201

**PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT**

**FROM:** Priya Anand, Responsible Partner (FL Bar No. 0087451) Douglas Carmichael, Billing Partner (FL Bar No. 0093217)
